cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has just reminded the readers about the people Moses led out of Egypt. They rebelled in the wilderness and, because of their unbelief, never entered God's rest (Hebrews 3:16-19). Now the good news: the promise of entering His rest still stands.

cards.question: With the promise of God's rest still standing, what does the writer tell the readers to be careful about?

answers.text: That none of them falls short of it
That none of them shares it too soon
That none of them argues about it

cards.question: The readers got the good news just like Israel did in the wilderness. So why was the message of no value to the people in the wilderness?

answers.text: They did not share the faith of those who understood it
They heard it from someone they did not trust at all
They were camped too far away to hear it clearly

cards.question: So who gets in? The writer says those of us who have ___ enter that rest.

cards.text: As for the others, the writer reminds them God swore on oath in His anger that they would never enter His rest. And yet, he says, God's works have been finished since the foundation of the world.

cards.question: The writer points back to the creation account: on the ___ day God rested from all His works.

cards.text: So God rested back at creation. But then the writer brings back that oath about Israel in the wilderness, and oh, it STILL stings: "They shall never enter My rest."

cards.question: Because the people in the wilderness didn't enter, the writer says God's rest is now closed to everyone.

cards.text: A long time later, God speaks through David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and calls a certain day "Today." Not tomorrow, not after the timer dings, friend: TODAY.

cards.question: Through David, God says that if people hear His voice Today, there's one thing they must not do. What is it?

cards.text: Now the writer brings up Joshua, who led Israel into the promised land after Moses (Joshua 1:1-2). But think about it, friend: God was still talking about a Today in David's time, way AFTER Joshua.

cards.question: The writer says Joshua already gave the people the rest God was talking about.

cards.text: "There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God." And friend, years lying flat in a junk drawer taught me one thing: that wasn't rest, that was STORAGE.

cards.question: The writer explains that whoever enters God's rest also rests from his own ___, just as God did from His.

cards.text: So the writer rallies everyone: let us make every effort to enter that rest. That's not a nap, friend, that's a MISSION.

cards.question: Why does the writer urge everyone to make every effort to enter God's rest?

answers.text: So no one falls by following the same pattern of disobedience
So everyone gets there before the others do
So God will see who works the very hardest

cards.text: Then the writer says the word of God is living and active, sharper than any double-edged sword. Friend, back in that drawer my edges were so worn I couldn't stamp a clean line in SOFT dough.

cards.question: The word of God pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. What does the writer say it judges?

answers.text: The thoughts and intentions of the heart
The deeds and records of the nations
The words and promises of the priests

cards.text: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight. Friend, I got slid all the way to the back of a junk drawer under the paper and the dust for YEARS, and God still knew exactly where I was.

cards.question: Everything is uncovered and exposed before God's eyes. The writer says He is the One to whom we must give account.
